kpis.label: Reference price
kpis.sub: Rs 90.10 = Sep-2025 preferential issue at Rs 901 per Rs 10 share, adjusted for the 4:1 bonus and 1:2 split (pp. 125-127). It is a reference point, not a price band.

focus.title: Current vs deferred tax
focus.detail: Current tax 21.0% of cumulative PBT (183.53 / 871.88 = 21.0%); deferred tax was 25.13 of the 83.16 FY26 charge (30.2%). Cash tax is below the 25.17% statutory rate, consistent with accelerated depreciation on a large capex base.

focus.title: Related-party capex & subsidiaries
focus.detail: Solar panels and installation bought from related party Climate Detox Renewables: Rs 201.89 m in FY25 (27.9% of FY25 purchase of fixed assets, Rs 724.27 m). Proceeds go to the subsidiary JB rPET as equity or debt, mode not decided (p. 115); the subsidiary is wholly owned so there is no minority leakage. Loans to the subsidiary Rs 159.22 m (FY26) and Rs 265.00 m (FY25), with Rs 250.00 m converted to equity in FY26.

focus.title: Revaluation reserve
focus.detail: Revaluation reserve (Ind AS deemed-cost uplift of PPE) Rs 614.81 m = 22.5% of total equity of Rs 2,737.70 m. The issuer's own net worth, NAV and RoNW exclude it (net worth Rs 2,122.89 m), but total equity, debt-to-equity and the balance sheet include it.

focus.title: Contingent liabilities
focus.detail: Contingent liabilities Rs 1,333.86 m = 62.8% of ICDR net worth (Rs 2,122.89 m) or 48.7% of total equity. Rs 1,155.20 m are corporate guarantees for the consolidated subsidiary's own loans (the risk factor on subsidiary guarantees states Rs 1,055.20 m while the contingent liabilities table states Rs 1,155.20 m, a Rs 100.00 m difference the DRHP does not reconcile), so most of it is already in borrowings. Tax disputes Rs 76.07 m net of pre-deposits. Materiality threshold for litigation is Rs 10.70 m (lowest of three tests).

focus.title: Auditor qualifications / changes
focus.detail: No qualification; FY24 special-purpose consolidated report carries an emphasis of matter on basis of accounting (p. 43). Auditor change: DSI & Co resigned 12-Dec-2024 citing other professional commitments; Singhi & Co appointed 20-Mar-2025 to fill the casual vacancy and re-appointed 30-Sep-2025 for four years (p. 85).

focus.title: CARO / audit trail
focus.detail: CARO 2020 clause (iii)(h)(vi): audit trail feature not enabled at database level for the accounting software, reported for the consolidated, standalone and subsidiary FY26 reports. Management says it is implementing it. No adjustment to the restated numbers.

focus.title: Valuation model guard
focus.detail: AMBER: DCF and relative diverge by -79.9% - the divergence is the finding; name its cause

focus.title: Valuation model guard
focus.detail: AMBER: TV above 75% of EV - DCF is mostly a terminal guess

focus.title: Valuation model guard
focus.detail: RED: terminal ROIC below WACC - growth destroys value

comfort.title: Bonus issue / share-count consistency
comfort.detail: 4:1 bonus (28-Apr-2026) and 1:2 split (24-Apr-2026) are reflected: EPS 1.31 / 1.24 / 1.38 and NAV 12.34 use 171,988,460 shares for all years. The FY26 balance sheet still shows 17,198,846 shares of Rs 10 (capital Rs 171.99 m), which is the pre-bonus count and is a presentation point only.

comfort.title: Cash flow vs profit
comfort.detail: CFO positive in all three years: 156.84 / 315.32 / 820.93 (Rs m, FY24/25/26); cumulative CFO/PAT = 201%. CFO is struck before interest (Rs 602.92 m paid over three years); after interest the ratio is about 108%. FY26 CFO includes a Rs 541.21 m inventory release after a Rs 701.65 m build in FY25. Capex over three years was Rs 2,925.09 m, funded by debt and equity.

comfort.title: Goodwill vs tangible equity
comfort.detail: No goodwill. Other intangible assets nil at 31-Mar-2026; Rs 0.71 m under development.

comfort.title: Monitoring agency
comfort.detail: Monitoring agency to be appointed before the RHP is filed, as the offer exceeds Rs 1,000 m. Objects repay bank and NBFC loans only; no related-party loan is listed for repayment (pp. 112-113). Personal guarantees of promoters, directors and relatives support the loans to be prepaid (p. 334), so repayment may release them: an indirect promoter benefit.

comfort.title: Eligibility re-computation
comfort.detail: Re-performed Reg 6(1): operating profit 585.80 / 509.29 / 387.58 Rs m reproduces from PBT (308.08 less other income 10.80 plus finance cost 277.79 plus exceptional 10.73 = 585.80); three-year average 494.22 vs Rs 150 m minimum. Net worth 2,122.89 / 1,401.00 / 1,019.02. Monetary assets 2.17% of net tangible assets. KPI EBITDA (898.76) reproduces from the P&L.

comfort.title: Firm means of finance
comfort.detail: Entire requirement is met from net proceeds, so no separate 75% means-of-finance tie-up is needed; issuer states compliance with Reg 7(1)(e).

strengths: Second largest Indian PET recycler by installed capacity, 180,360 MTPA at Aug-2026; source: issuer-commissioned report (p. 220)
Only Indian player with mechanical and chemical recycling; food-grade resin approved by two global beverage firms (pp. 224, 226)
CFO positive each year: 156.84 / 315.32 / 820.93 Rs m (p. 73)
Net debt / EBITDA 5.25x to 3.40x over FY24-26 (p. 122)
Litigation materiality threshold of Rs 10.70 m is the lowest of three tests (p. 384)
weaknesses: PAT flat: Rs 211.32 m FY24 vs Rs 224.92 m FY26 (p. 72)
RPSF still 55.12% of revenue; Chemically Recycled Resins revenue fell 23.3% in FY26 (p. 223)
Revenue per tonne fell 2.4% in FY26 while volume rose 18.4% (pp. 122, 72)
Audit trail not enabled at database level, FY26 (p. 43)
opportunities: Mandatory recycled content in rigid packaging of 30% / 40% / 50% / 60% for FY26-FY29 (p. 222)
Indian food-grade rPET resin volume 300.0 KT in FY26 to 2,210.7 KT by FY31, issuer-commissioned estimate (p. 187)
Food-grade capacity raised to 56,160 MTPA in Aug-2026; FY26 utilisation of this line was 52.47% (pp. 24, 227)
Rs 3,200 m debt repayment against Rs 3,493.95 m outstanding on listed loans (p. 113)
threats: Corporate guarantees of Rs 1,155.20 m for the subsidiary's loans (p. 74)
Raw material (PET waste) has no long-term supply contracts (p. 228)
Fire at the plant on 04-Dec-2025; insurance claim under assessment (p. 26)
Ganesha Ecosphere, a larger listed rival, runs 64,500 TPA of food-grade capacity (p. 188)
Imports were 11.02% of FY26 COGS, up from 1.86% (p. 244)
